The missing source is almost certainly this file:
PowerShell%APPDATA%\Docker\last-start-linux-daemon.json
For your user that expands to:
PowerShellC:\Users\<YOU>\AppData\Roaming\Docker\last-start-linux-daemon.json
If you ever switched to Windows containers, also check:
PowerShellC:\Users\<YOU>\AppData\Roaming\Docker\last-start-windows-daemon.json
Docker Desktop’s uninstall/cleanup logs explicitly treat these as separate daemon-state files alongside ~\.docker\daemon.json; old and current diagnostic bundles also gather last-start-linux-daemon.json as a Docker Desktop daemon config artifact. That matches your symptom: you delete ~\.docker\daemon.json, Docker Desktop reconstructs it from a remembered “last start” daemon config. Docker Community Forums+2GitHub+2
It is not the installer binary. It is also not primarily the WSL VHDX. The WSL disk at %LOCALAPPDATA%\Docker\wsl stores Docker Desktop’s WSL2 backend data; Docker’s own docs say that is the WSL2 engine data location and should be moved via Docker Desktop’s Disk image location setting. That is different from the host-side Docker Engine JSON config at $HOME\.docker\daemon.json. Docker Documentation+1
Run this, with Docker Desktop fully stopped:
PowerShell# Stop Docker Desktop completelyStop-Process -Name "Docker Desktop" -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinueStop-Process -Name "com.docker.backend" -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinueStop-Process -Name "com.docker.proxy" -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinueStop-Process -Name "com.docker.service" -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinuewsl --shutdown# Remove the daemon config that Docker Desktop keeps regeneratingRemove-Item "$env:USERPROFILE\.docker\daemon.json" -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue# Remove the hidden "last started daemon config" sourceRemove-Item "$env:APPDATA\Docker\last-start-linux-daemon.json" -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinueRemove-Item "$env:APPDATA\Docker\last-start-windows-daemon.json" -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue# Optional: remove other stale Docker Desktop daemon snapshots if presentRemove-Item "$env:APPDATA\Docker\last-start-daemon.json" -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinueRemove-Item "$env:APPDATA\Docker\linux-daemon.json" -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinueRemove-Item "$env:APPDATA\Docker\windows-daemon.json" -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue# Start Docker Desktop againStart-Process "C:\Program Files\Docker\Docker\Docker Desktop.exe"
Then verify:
PowerShelldocker info --format '{{.DockerRootDir}}'Get-Content "$env:USERPROFILE\.docker\daemon.json" -Raw
Expected for Linux containers / WSL2:
/var/lib/docker
and the recreated daemon.json should not contain:
JSON"data-root": "D:\\Code\\docker-data"
If it still comes back, prove the remaining source with this exact search after stopping Docker again:
PowerShellStop-Process -Name "Docker Desktop" -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinueStop-Process -Name "com.docker.backend" -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinuewsl --shutdown$needle = @( 'D:\Code\docker-data', 'D:\\Code\\docker-data', 'D:/Code/docker-data', 'data-root', 'linuxDockerdConfiguration', 'windowsDockerdConfiguration')$roots = @( "$env:USERPROFILE\.docker", "$env:APPDATA\Docker", "$env:APPDATA\Docker Desktop", "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Docker", "C:\ProgramData\Docker", "C:\ProgramData\DockerDesktop")foreach ($root in $roots) { if (Test-Path $root) { Write-Host "`n### $root" Get-ChildItem $root -Recurse -Force -File -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Where-Object { $_.Length -lt 50MB } | Select-String -Pattern $needle -SimpleMatch -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select-Object Path, LineNumber, Line }}
But given your new clue, the file you missed is:
PowerShell$env:APPDATA\Docker\last-start-linux-daemon.json
Delete that plus ~\.docker\daemon.json, then restart Docker Desktop.
